title: FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint — working notes (daily log + open questions)
content:
Doc purpose
- This is the messy working doc for the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint.
- Daily notes (what ran, what broke, what we learned), open questions, and “pending decisions” that should become ADRs.
- Canonical status for the benchmark lab runs lives in the sheet: shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/fp8-int8-benchmark-matrix

Quick links (pin these)
- Sprint charter (Confluence): fp8-int8-benchmarking-sprint-charter
- Methodology / pitfalls (Confluence): benchmark-methodology-fp8-int8-kernels
- Metrics definitions ADR (Confluence): adr-quant-benchmark-metrics-and-definitions
- FP8 policy ADR (Confluence): adr-fp8-format-and-accumulation-policy (draft)
- Runbook (Confluence): runbook-running-benchmarks-in-benchmark-lab
- Profiling cheatsheet (Confluence): fp8-int8-profiling-cheatsheet
- Linear umbrella: ENG-24810

People / owners (for quick paging)
- Harness + matrix owner: Rina
- Runtime perf architect / “stop us from lying with stats”: Noah
- FP8/INT8 kernels: Grace (FP8 attention), Isabella (microbench)
- Auto-selection + logging: Yuki
- Scheduler experiments: Sofia (lead), Lena, Marcus, Julian
- Applied ML guardrails: Arjun, Priyanka, Jonas
- Perf lab reliability: Sean
- Dashboards: Allison
- Release / canary gates: Connor
- Program mgmt: Talia

Baseline plan (what we’re measuring)
- Microbench
  - FP8 attention (prefill + decode kernels where applicable)
  - INT8 GEMM hot spots (MLP + projection) + conversion/dequant overhead
  - KV cache interaction points (scale/zero-point conversions)
- End-to-end
  - TTFT (prefill latency) + TPOT (time per output token) split by phase
  - Tokens/sec (throughput), and p50/p95/p99 across repeated runs
  - Scheduler queue wait times: histogram split by {prefill, decode} x {FP16, FP8, INT8}

Run hygiene reminders (write here when we violate them)
- GPU clocks must be locked for any “publishable” results (otherwise huge noise)
- Warmup: minimum 5–10 iterations or until kernel cache / autotune stabilizes
- Run repeats: aim 10+ for microbench, 5+ for end-to-end; record all raw runs, don’t cherry-pick
- Pin: runtime commit + container digest + driver/CUDA + NCCL where relevant

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Daily notes

2025-10-01 (Wed) — Kickoff + align on matrix
- Kickoff thread in #eng-runtime (1730201123): initial model list + GPU list + owners.
- Top hosted model families to include (tentative): Llama-family, Qwen-family, Mistral-family.
- Workload buckets we need:
  - Prefill-heavy: long input (4k–16k prompt), short decode (64–256)
  - Decode-heavy: shorter prompt (256–1k), longer decode (512–2k)
  - Streaming chat: concurrency + TTFT/TPOT is the main story
- Decision (informal): Treat TTFT as first-class for streaming; don’t let tokens/sec win at the cost of TTFT regressions.
- TODO: Confirm GPU availability for H200 + L40S in perf lab (ENG-24813) and who gets priority windows.

2025-10-02 (Thu) — Environment pinning + first harness PRs
- ENG-24812 in progress: pin container digest + driver/CUDA version in perf-lab build.
- Harness PRs queued:
  - benchmark-lab#412 (config schema + validation)
  - benchmark-lab#414 (workload presets + experiment matrix generator)
- Perf-lab reliability note (Sean): nodes show contention during US morning hours; try reserving dedicated window; track if noisy neighbors correlate with variance.
- Noise investigation started in #eng-runtime (1730229044): warmup + clocks + container pinning checklist drafted.

2025-10-03 (Fri) — Baselines start + immediate weirdness on INT8
- First baseline runs (A100 + H100) started for INT8 and FP8 paths.
- Observed: INT8 sometimes slower than FP16 for certain shapes (decode-heavy) on A100.
- Hypothesis: auto-selector is choosing FP16 kernel due to shape guard bug OR INT8 path paying conversion overhead every step.
- Action:
  - Yuki to add kernel-selection logging improvements (ENG-24814 / redwood#10621 + redwood#10631)
  - Grace/Isabella to microbench conversion+dequant overhead; isolate from GEMM itself.
- Mateo email mid-sprint readout draft referenced (internal): thread_2025-10-03_fp8-int8-sprint-readout (note: we should mirror key points into final report later).

2025-10-06 (Mon) — FP8 prefill regression shows up on long-context
- From baseline end-to-end: FP8 path has a TTFT regression on long-context prompts (8k–16k) on H100.
- It’s not just a small bump; looks like a step-function at certain alignment boundaries.
- Profiling notes thread started (1730245510): Nsight command snippets + initial timelines.
- Hypothesis list:
  1) Alignment/stride handling bug causing extra loads / misaligned vectorization
  2) Kernel launch config not matching long-seq shapes; tile sizes bad for long context
  3) Prefill using fallback kernel unexpectedly (autoselect mismatch)
- Action items:
  - Grace to reproduce with microbench harness; isolate to attention prefill kernel.
  - Yuki to ensure chosen kernel + shapes are logged in tracing spans for this run.

2025-10-07 (Tue) — Kernel logging lands + first reproducible profiles
- Redwood PR redwood#10621 merged (kernel-selection + quant-mode tracing spans behind flag).
- Redwood PR redwood#10631 drafted (structured perf log events JSON): phase breakdown + GPU clocks + kernel IDs.
- We captured first “good” Nsight Systems trace:
  - Artifact location (internal): gs://redwood-perf-artifacts/quant-sprint/2025-10-07/h100_fp8_prefill_longctx_run3/
  - Notes: trace shows extra memcpy-ish activity around prefill; unclear if real or tool overhead.
- Reminder: Make sure tracing spans flag is OFF for baseline perf runs; only enable for attribution runs.

2025-10-08 (Wed) — INT8 autoselector bug confirmed
- Yuki confirmed a mismatch: for certain INT8 shapes, auto-selector chooses FP16 kernel (wrong family) due to a missing guard.
- Redwood PR redwood#10625 opened: “Fix: kernel auto-selector incorrectly choosing FP16 kernel for specific INT8 shapes; adds guard + unit test.”
- Microbench sanity:
  - When forced to INT8 kernel, GEMM is faster as expected, but end-to-end still mixed because conversion overhead is non-trivial.
- Action:
  - Keep both views in report: “INT8 math kernel wins” vs “pipeline overhead can dominate.”

2025-10-09 (Thu) — Scheduler experiments start (tail latency focus)
- Sofia/Lena/Marcus set up scheduler experiment matrix (ENG-24816): prefill/decode interleaving policy vs batch size caps.
- Theory: quantized decode under mixed prompt lengths creates tail-lat spikes due to oversized decode batches.
- Redwood PR redwood#10624 opened: “Scheduler: batch-size cap override for quantized decode to reduce tail latency under mixed prompt lengths.”
- Open question: do we want cap keyed by quant mode, by model family, or by GPU SKU? (Probably quant mode + GPU class; model family only if proven.)

2025-10-10 (Fri) — Release train coordination + gating
- Connor email thread: thread_2025-10-10_quant-changes-release-train
  - Ask: which PRs are safe to land for next runtime release vs hold.
  - Release checklist request: perf-canary must be green on selected GPUs + correctness drift checks for INT8.
- Perf-canary work:
  - perf-canary#188: new quant-perf nightly job (selected GPUs)
  - perf-canary#189: comparator improvements (outlier handling)
- Proposed gate philosophy (draft, not final):
  - Block release if: p95 TTFT regression > threshold on H100 streaming scenario OR correctness drift check fails.
  - Allow with mitigation if: throughput regression isolated to A100 microbench with known variance AND end-to-end unaffected.

2025-10-13 (Mon) — FP8 regression root cause + fix in progress
- Grace found likely alignment handling issue in FP8 prefill path for long-context.
- Redwood PR redwood#10630 opened: “Bugfix: FP8 prefill path incorrect alignment handling on long-context prompts; targeted regression test.”
- Also in flight: redwood#10622 (FP8 attention tuning for H100/H200): tile sizes / launch config.
- Early retest on H100 (single node, clocks locked): TTFT improves vs baseline FP8 longctx; need repeated runs to confirm.
- TODO: Ensure we test on H200 too once provisioned. (ENG-24813 status?)

2025-10-14 (Tue) — Correctness / drift guardrails + L40S caveat
- Priyanka/Jonas/Arjun aligned on drift checks scope for CI:
  - Redwood PR redwood#10627: numeric drift checks for INT8/FP8 vs FP16 baseline on small prompt set; gating policy in CI.
  - Still need to decide the “acceptable drift” thresholds for hosted. (See Open Questions below.)
- L40S issue:
  - Intermittent correctness failures tied to a fused op on L40S.
  - Redwood PR redwood#10635: hotfix to disable on L40S (GPU-conditional) + tests.
- Dashboard work:
  - observability-pack#97 adds panels split by {quant mode, chosen kernel, model family} and links to runbook.
  - Allison requests tags consistency: ensure structured perf log includes gpu_sku, runtime_commit, quant_mode, kernel_id, workload_preset.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Profiling notes (scratch)

Commands / recipes (from cheatsheet + our tweaks)
- Nsight Systems (end-to-end):
  - nsys profile -t cuda,nvtx,osrt -s none -o run1 --force-overwrite=true --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi ./bench_runner ...
- Nsight Compute (kernel focus):
  - ncu --set full --kernel-name-base demangled --launch-skip 5 --launch-count 20 -o ncu_run ./microbench ...

Artifacts (internal pointers)
- H100 FP8 prefill longctx traces:
  - gs://redwood-perf-artifacts/quant-sprint/2025-10-07/h100_fp8_prefill_longctx_run3/
  - gs://redwood-perf-artifacts/quant-sprint/2025-10-13/h100_fp8_prefill_fix_candidate_run2/
- INT8 shape mismatch repro logs:
  - gs://redwood-perf-artifacts/quant-sprint/2025-10-08/a100_int8_autoselect_mismatch/

Notes on interpreting timelines (things we keep confusing)
- TTFT inflation can be from:
  - actual prefill kernel slower
  - increased queue wait before prefill starts (scheduler)
  - hidden sync points (mem alloc, stream sync) that appear as “blank” on GPU timeline
- When spans/logging are enabled, we may perturb results; do not compare traced runs to untraced baselines.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Open questions / decisions pending ADRs

1) FP8 format + accumulation policy (ADR needed)
- e4m3 vs e5m2: default per GPU? per model family? (Need to avoid per-model explosion if possible.)
- Accumulation type: FP16 vs FP32 for key layers?
- Scaling strategy: per-tensor vs per-channel, and what’s “safe” for hosted quality.
- Owner: Grace + Arjun; reviewer: Noah; target: convert current notes into adr-fp8-format-and-accumulation-policy.

2) Correctness guardrails (what blocks a release?)
- Drift thresholds: what metric do we gate on?
  - Options we discussed: relative L2 on logits, top-k agreement, exact-match on short deterministic prompts, or embedding cosine drift.
- Are thresholds uniform across all hosted models? Or per family?
- Where to run: CI subset only vs nightly full?
- Owner: Priyanka + Jonas; release input: Connor.

3) “Success metric” hierarchy for reporting (for sprint report)
- We keep mixing goals: TTFT vs TPOT vs tokens/sec.
- Proposal (from Slack 1730298812):
  - Streaming chat: prioritize p95 TTFT, then p95 TPOT, then throughput.
  - Batch offline: prioritize throughput + cost proxy; TTFT less important.
- Need to formalize in adr-quant-benchmark-metrics-and-definitions (aggregation rules too).

4) Auto-selector policy + fallback behavior
- Should we ever allow “silent fallback to FP16” in quant mode if INT8 kernel missing/slow?
  - Good for safety, bad for perf predictability + benchmarking clarity.
- At minimum: emit explicit “fallback_reason” in logs.
- Owner: Yuki.

5) Scheduler knobs defaults (batch-size caps, interleaving)
- If we ship quant-mode-specific batch caps, are we comfortable with different latency/throughput tradeoffs by quant mode?
- Need to test impact on mixed workloads (prefill heavy + decode heavy simultaneously).
- Owner: Sofia / Lena.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
To-do / action list (rolling)
- [Rina] Keep benchmark matrix sheet updated; mark runs invalid if clocks not locked / wrong container.
- [Sean] Confirm perf-lab dedicated windows; document “noisy neighbor” mitigation; update infra ticket if needed.
- [Noah] Review comparator stats approach in perf-canary#189; ensure we’re not masking real regressions.
- [Grace] Land FP8 prefill alignment fix (redwood#10630) + validate on H100 and H200.
- [Yuki] Ensure kernel-selection logging is low overhead and captured in structured perf logs; finalize redwood#10631.
- [Isabella] Extend microbench suite to include conversion overhead metrics for INT8 path (isolate conversion vs GEMM vs memory).
- [Marcus/Julian] Export scheduler queue wait histograms by phase/quant mode (redwood#10632) and validate panels.
- [Allison] Finalize dashboard spec tags (quant-perf-dashboard-spec) and confirm ingestion format from benchmark-lab#415.
- [Connor] Define initial regression thresholds allowlist (Confluence: quantized-kernel-regression-thresholds) for canary gating.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Notes for final sprint report (capture as we go; don’t trust memory later)
- We must clearly separate:
  1) Kernel-level speedups (microbench)
  2) End-to-end improvements (TTFT/TPOT) which include scheduler + overhead
  3) Reliability of results (variance, pinned env)
- Call out “gotchas” we hit:
  - Autoselector choosing wrong family for INT8 shapes
  - FP8 long-context alignment bug
  - Perf-lab variance due to clocks / contention
  - L40S fused op correctness flake
- Include at least one “before/after” story where we can attribute causality (fix -> metric delta -> trace evidence).

Appendix: Meeting notes scratchpad (lightweight)
- Weekly checkpoint agenda:
  - What is green? what is red?
  - Any metrics we’re tempted to ignore?
  - Are we on track for publishable methodology?
- Reminder: if we change a default, we need:
  - rollback knob
  - canary cohort plan
  - correctness gate (or explicit waiver) and sign-off
